analysis:
This PR changes documentation only.

cli-reference.md head 1804-1810 adds a paragraph: on a Mac running a cluster service, `darkbloom update` asks that service's supervisor to restart into the installed release together with the other Mac, after the pair has drained. A deferral exits 1. Head 2148 extends the `auto_update` row to cover the pair's coordinated update at its update slot.

In cluster-always-on.md (metadata only; the patch excerpt is truncated), the supervisor now updates Darkbloom on both Macs. This replaces the earlier note that nothing updates cluster Macs automatically. The new section covering head lines 115-195 says the supervisor reuses AutoUpdateController with the single-Mac gate: auto_update and DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK.

Security relevance:
- The update path still states that bundle, binary and metallib hashes are verified before replacement (head 1801-1802, unchanged).
- Coordinated pair auto-update is new update-trigger behavior on cluster Macs. It is relevant to T-013 and T-043 (watchdog/rollback, replaceable binary) and to A-011 and A-017.

The docs claim the existing verified updater sequence is reused. No supplied source (UpdateCommand.swift, ClusterServiceCommand.swift, ClusterServiceUpdateRequest) shows how the inter-Mac restart request is authenticated or whether the peer independently verifies the installed release. Whether a peer Mac or a local process can trigger or force a restart/update on the other Mac cannot be determined from docs alone.

The threat model has no entry for the two-Mac cluster supervisor update channel. Integration or source review should check:
- the authentication of the supervisor update request;
- that each Mac performs its own hash and signature verification;
- deferral and rollback behavior.

The docs also don't show whether `--force` semantics carry over to the pair.

No concrete regression is evidenced in the docs, so there are no findings.
